FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council. The Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard is given in Annex E. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, t-he final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 14336 : 1996

Indian Standard

SHIPBUILDING - DECK COVERING MATERIALS - SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE 4.2 Resistance to Sea Water

This standard lays down the requirements of deck covering materials to be used on board ships. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards adjuncts to this Standard : IS No. Title 1460 : 1974 3461: 1980 3462 : 1986 11239 (Part 14) : 1992 13286 : 1992 are necessary

When tested in accordance with Annex B the material shall not show more than a very slight colour change. 4.3 Colour Fastness in Absence of Light When tested in accordance with Annex C no change in colour shall-be apparent. 4.4 Fire Characteristics 4.4.1 Smoke Index Index to be less than 130 when no hologens when tested in accordance with IS 14307 (Parts 1 to 4) : 1995. 4.5 Toxicity Index Index to be less than 1.5 with no hologens when tested in accordance with IS 14307 (Parts 1 to 4) : 1995. 4.6 Oxygen Index Index to be more than 22 when tested in accordance with IS 11239 (Part 14) : 1992. 4.7 Surface Spread of Flame Not worse than class 2 when calculated in accordance with IS 13286 : 1992. 4.8 Chlorine Evolution When tested in accordance with Annex D the chlorine content shall not be more than 5 per cent when heated to a temperature of 200�C for a period of 30 minutes. 5 TYPETESTS 5.1 All the test specified in 4.1 to 4.8, in addition to any type tests specified in IS 3461: 1980 and IS 3462 : 1986 shall constitute type tests. 6 PACKAGING AND MARKING 6.1 Bach package constituting a consignment shall be legibly and durably marked as follows : a) Source of manufacture and date of manufacture/batch number; and b) Size of tiles, width of roll, thickness and colourjpattern.

Diesel fuels (second revision) Specification for PVC-asbestos floor tiles (first revision) Specification for unback flexible PVC flooring (second revision) Method of test for cellular thermal insulation materials : Part 14 Determination of flammability of oxygen index Surface spread of flame for thermal insulation materials - Method of test

14307 Shipbuilding - Deck covering, (Parts 1 to.4) : thermal and acoustic insulation 1995 materials - Methods of tests
3 MATERIALS

Following materials shall be used : a) PVA tiles/rolls conforming to IS 3461: 1980. b) PVC tiles/rolls conforming to IS 3462 : 1986. 4 TESTS In addition to tests specified in specification IS 3461 : 1980 and IS 3462 : 1986, the tiles/rolls shall also comply with the requirements given under 4.1 to 4.8. 4.1 Resistance to Diesel Contaminations When tested in accordance with Annex A of this standard the material shall not break, crack or show any signs of failure. 4.1.1 The material shall not show more than a very slight change in colour when compared with its control as at A-~(C).

A-3 PROCEDURE

a) Two test specimens of 150 mm x 75 mm
shall be cut from each of two 300 mm x 300 mm pieces of flooring, such that in two specimens the longer dimension is parallel to the grains and is at right angle to the grains in the other two. Four identical specimens shall be cut as controls and retained in the laboratory. Freely suspend the test specimens in diesel held in a suitable size container, such that they are completely immersed for a period of

4

e)

b)

7 days. At the end of the test period remove the test pieces from the diesel and wash twice in a warm 10 per cent solution of the detergent in water, wipe dry and then place in an oven at 80�C for 7 days along with the controls. At the end of that period remove all the test specimens and allow to condition for 24 hours under normal ambient conditions. The test piece is then compared with its control, for any change in colour, in the viewing cabinet using artificial daylight and additional artificial daylight bulbs. Strips of 150 mm x 50 mm shall be cut from the centre portion of each test piece. Bend each strip by hand over a mandrel 40 mm in diameter, with the wearing surface outwards, through an arc of 180 at an even speed in approximately three seconds. Examine the bent portion in good lighting conditions and under magnification of X4 for cracks, breaks or other signs of failure.

ANNEX B (Chse 4.2)

RESISTANCE TO SEA WATER B-l APPARATUS a) b) Suitable size container. Viewing cabinet. gitudinal axis. One test piece from each specimen shall be freely suspended to a depth of 150 mm in sea water for a period of ten days, whilst the other is stored in the laboratory with full access to diffused daylight. At the end of this test period remove the test pieces from the sea water, wash in fresh waterto remove all traces of sea water, wipe dry and leave to condition for twenty four hours under ambient conditions. The immersed test piece is * then compared with the unimmersed test piece, in the viewing cabinet using standard artificial daylight and additional artificial daylight bulbs; any differences in colour is recorded.

COLOUR FASTNESS IN ABSENCE OF LIGIIT C-l APPARATUS a) b) A box of suitable dimensions constructed so as to exclude light. Viewing cabinet. 2 C-2 PROCEDURE a) Two pieces 150 mm x 100 mm shall be cut from a specimen of vinyl flooring. One piece shall be placed in a light-proof box for a

IS 14336:1996 period of 28 days whilst the other piece is stored in the laboratory with full access to diffused daylight. After 28 days the two pieces are compared in a viewingcabinet using standard artificial daylight and additional artificial daylight bulbs, and any differences in colour recorded.

ANNEX

D

(Clause 4.8)
CEILORINE EVOLUTION TEST D-l APPARATUS a) b) c) d) Round bottom flask. Thermostatically controlled oil bath. Apparatus for pre-heating nitrogen. Weighing balance. D-3 PROCEDURE D-3.1 Ten grams of `PVA/PVC' material to be heated in a round bottom flask fitted with two glass tubes immersed in an oil bath. Through one of the tubes, pre-heated nitrogen is allowed to pass through the flask. Oil bath is to be maintained at required temperature for 30 minutes. Gas evolved is carried by nitrogen into an absorbing tower filled with distilled water. In order to determine the HCl content the solution is titrated against 0.1 NNaOH solution. From the quantity of NaOH required for neutralisation, chlorine content shall be calculated.

D-2 REAGENTS a) b) Standard Sodium Hydroxide Solution - 0.1 N. Nitrogen Gas.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under ihe Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Additions'.
